newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ekran says drops planned brokerage buy.
newsitem.headline: Ekran says drops planned brokerage buy.

text.p: Malaysian infrastructure developer Ekran Bhd said on Friday it had cancelled plans to buy brokerage house Upen Securities Sdn Bhd.

"Ekran... wishes to announce that the company had mutually agreed... with the vendors of Upen Securities Sdn Bhd, to terminate the proposed acquisition by Ekran of 20 million shares... representing the entire share capital of Upen," said Ekran in a statement circulated on Monday.
No reason was given for the termination.
Ekran had originally planned to buy the brokerage firm in July, in conjunction with a restructuring of Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing's holdings.
The company had said in July it would acquire two companies holding a 49 percent stake in PWE Industries Bhd and a 32.29 percent stake in Granite Industries Bhd for 924.45 million ringgit.
Ekran, PWE and Granite are all controlled by Ting and are involved in the construction of the $6.18 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam in Srawak state on Borneo island.
The proposed acquisitions were announced following the undersubcription of an Ekran rights issue to finance the project.
